South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index crashed 9.99 percent on June 23, closing at 8,203.84 after shedding 910.71 points, a one-day collapse so steep it triggered a market-wide circuit breaker that halted trading for 20 minutes. The plunge was led by the country’s two semiconductor giants and amounted to one of the sharpest single-session declines in years.

Why it matters
Two companies now account for nearly half the KOSPI’s value and about 70% of its 2026 gains, so a wobble in AI-memory sentiment becomes a national market event — and a stress test for whether this year’s AI rally is built on earnings or on extrapolation. The speed of the circuit-breaker halt, and the scale of foreign selling, show how a single-day repricing of the AI trade can ricochet from New York to Seoul before most investors have woken up.

Samsung Electronics fell roughly 12.3 percent and SK Hynix about 12.5 percent, as foreign investors dumped a net 5.79 trillion won — around $3.8 billion — of Korean shares. The selling was severe enough to activate a sidecar mechanism that briefly suspended program trading after KOSPI 200 futures tumbled.

The immediate trigger came from overseas. A heavy overnight selloff in US technology stocks, combined with renewed worries that the Federal Reserve under new chair Kevin Warsh may raise rates again to curb inflation, hammered semiconductor sentiment across Asia. Compounding the damage, South Korea was left out of an upcoming MSCI review for inclusion in its Developed Markets index, removing a catalyst many investors had been positioning for.

The crash exposed how concentrated the Korean market has become. Together, Samsung and SK Hynix account for nearly half of the KOSPI’s total value — about 48 percent — and have contributed roughly 70 percent of the index’s gains in 2026. SK Hynix alone had climbed nearly 190 percent on the year before the drop, driven by insatiable demand for the high-bandwidth memory that powers AI data centers.

That concentration cuts both ways. The same names that drove the index to records on June 22 dragged it down the next session, and when sentiment turned, there was little to cushion the fall. Analysts framed the move less as a verdict on the companies’ fundamentals — both remain highly profitable — than as a sudden reassessment of how much future success was already baked into their prices.

For all the drama, the rout did not erase the year. Even after the 10 percent fall, the KOSPI remained up roughly 80 percent for 2026, ranking it among the world’s best-performing major equity benchmarks. On June 24 the index rebounded about 3 percent to 8,471, as bargain hunters returned and Asian tech shares steadied.

The episode is a reminder that this year’s AI-driven rally, however well-grounded in real demand, has produced valuations sensitive to every shift in interest-rate expectations and every headline out of Wall Street. With memory makers booked to capacity and AI spending still climbing, the long-term story remains intact — but June 23 showed how violently the market can reprice that story in the space of a morning.

# Bitcoin slides 2% as Kospi Plunges 10% — BTC Drops to $63K

Bitcoin slid 2% after U.S. markets closed Monday, with South Korea's Kospi index leading Asian equities lower and pulling cryptos down alongside equities. BTC fell to $63,200 from nearly $65,000, a 2.7% decline that hit ether (ETH), XRP, solana (SOL), and the broader crypto market, ending the brief resilience the market showed earlier Monday as NVDA shares tanked on Wall Street.

The drop follows a sharp selloff in Asian stocks, as South Korea's Kospi index plummeted 10% to its lowest level since mid-April. The index has now dropped 25% from its mid-June peak, with semiconductor heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each falling about 12%, according to market reports.

## Market Drivers

The Kospi's collapse triggered a market-wide circuit breaker, halting trading for 20 minutes. Foreign investors dumped a net 5.79 trillion won (approximately $3.8 billion) in Korean shares, marking one of the sharpest single-session declines in years. The semiconductor sector led the rout, driven by concerns that the AI trade Rally may be losing steam.

Bitcoin has historically tracked equity-market volatility, but analysts suggest the correlation is often overstated. "BTC trades with equities when the stress is macro and rates-driven, and decouples when the stress is idiosyncratic to the equity market," Bitfinex analysts noted in a commentary.

## Regulatory Tailwinds Delayed

Away from the market selloff, the U.S. Senate has shelved the CLARITY Act to prioritize a Russia sanctions bill, pushing any vote on crypto regulatory clarity to next week before the August 8 recess. The legislation, aimed at delivering regulatory clarity and unlocking institutional buying for digital assets, now faces a delayed timeline.

## What Traders Should Watch

The Federal Reserve's利率 decision on Wednesday, followed by Core PCE and GDP data on Thursday, could significantly impact volatility across asset classes. "That makes Wednesday–Thursday the week's highest-volatility window for U.S. rate repricing," said Dessislava Ianeva, analyst at Nexo.

## Conclusion

Bitcoin slid 2% as risk-off sentiment swept through markets, with the Kospi's 10% plunge and semiconductor selloff dragging BTC down to $63,200. The correlation between bitcoin and equities remains complex, and traders should prepare for elevated volatility around the Fed's rate decision and key economic data this week.

**1. Why did Bitcoin drop 2%?**

Bitcoin fell as risk-off sentiment gripped markets following a 10% plunge in South Korea's Kospi index and a broader semiconductor selloff that hit equities worldwide.

**2. How much has BTC declined from its recent high?**

BTC fell to approximately $63,200 from nearly $65,000, a decline of about 2.7%.

**3. What is the Kospi index and why does it matter?**

The Kospi is South Korea's benchmark stock index. Its 10% plunge to the lowest level since mid-April signaled a broad risk-off move that affected crypto markets.

**4. What should traders watch this week?**

The Fed's rate decision on Wednesday and Core PCE and GDP data on Thursday are key events that could drive volatility across both equities and crypto.

The semiconductor sector led the rout, driven by concerns that the AI trade rally may be losing steam. "BTC trades with equities when the stress is macro and rates-driven, and decouples when the stress is idiosyncratic to the equity market," Bitfinex analysts noted in a commentary. The earnings-and-capital-expenditure debate is precisely an idiosyncratic stress, so the correlation between bitcoin and equities may be overstated on this data.

Together, Samsung and SK Hynix account for nearly half of the Kospi's total value, about 48 percent, and have contributed roughly 70% of the index's gains in 2026. SK Hynix alone had climbed nearly 190% on the year before the drop, driven by demand for high-bandwidth memory that powers AI data centers.

Away from the market selloff, the U.S. Senate has shelved the CLARITY Act to prioritize a Russia sanctions bill, pushing any vote on crypto regulatory clarity to next week before the August 8 recess. The legislation, aimed at delivering regulatory clarity and unlocking institutional buying for digital assets, now faces a delayed timeline. This leaves only the final days before the recess for a vote.

Markets are positioning for potential rate repricing, which could move bitcoin and other risk assets.

### Trading Implications

For crypto traders, the confluence of the equity selloff, semiconductor weakness, and upcoming Fed policy creates a complex environment.Bitcoin has shown resilience during AI selloffs in the past, but the high-stakes Fed meeting could determine the next directional move. Traders should monitor the rate decision and subsequent data releases carefully.

## Conclusion

Bitcoin slid 2% as risk-off sentiment swept through markets, with the Kospi's 10% plunge and semiconductor selloff dragging BTC down to $63,200. The correlation between bitcoin and equities remains complex, and traders should prepare for elevated volatility around the Fed's rate decision and key economic data this week. Watch for potential decoupling signals as the market digests the Fed's decision and incoming data.

Yes, the Fed's rate decision on Wednesday and key economic data on Thursday could drive significant volatility across both equities and crypto markets.

Analysts say the correlation is overstated. Bitcoin tends to trade with equities during macro and rates-driven stress, but decouples during idiosyncratic equity market stress like the current semiconductor selloff.
